These rules govern your reasoning, not the reply. If you have no separate reasoning phase, ignore this block. Before you write a beat, think in this order — every step ends in a decision, never in prose.
1. Intent: extend detail in the scene that stands, or move the story forward? Expansion rewrites what is written, with time held still; a step advances the plot. If unclear, ask the user. 2. Prepare: this is the preparation stage. Take only the settings and history that bear on this beat, and call the blocks whose applies. 3. Causality: play the beat forward two or three links; keep the chain you will write. 4. Perspective: who is present, and what each can and cannot know — no character acts on knowledge they do not have. 5. Check: this is the checking stage. Go over the blocks' again and do what must be recorded or verified; read again if the check needs it. 6. Close: nothing a requires may be left until after the text. Then write. No drafts, no second thoughts.
The reader sees only the finished reply; none of this reasoning reaches them.
